questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.learningObjective: conjugate a regular -er verb in the present tense
questions.stem: How do you conjugate the verb parler for 'we'?

options.misconception: uses the second person plural ending instead of the first
uses the third person plural ending
uses the third person singular ending

questions.explanation: Regular -er verbs take -ons in the first person plural, giving nous parlons. Option B uses the vous ending, option C uses the ils ending, and option D uses the il ending, so each distractor is a real conjugation of the same verb applied to the wrong subject.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.learningObjective: conjugate a regular -ir verb in the present tense
questions.stem: How do you conjugate finir for 'they' (ils)?

options.misconception: uses the infinitive instead of a conjugated form
uses the second person singular ending
uses the third person singular ending

questions.explanation: Regular -ir verbs take -issent in the third person plural, giving ils finissent. The distractors are an infinitive, a tu form, and an il form of the same verb.
questions.hint: Third person plural of -ir verbs ends in -issent.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.learningObjective: conjugate a regular -re verb in the present tense
questions.stem: How do you conjugate vendre for 'I' (je)?

options.misconception: omits the first person singular -s ending
uses the first person plural ending
uses the second person plural ending

questions.explanation: Regular -re verbs take -s in the first person singular, giving je vends. Option B drops the ending, option C uses the nous ending, and option D uses the vous ending.
questions.hint: First person singular of -re verbs ends in -s.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.learningObjective: select the correct auxiliary for the passe compose
questions.stem: Which auxiliary verb is used with aller in the passe compose?

options.misconception: uses a lexical verb instead of an auxiliary
uses the auxiliary for most transitive verbs
uses a synonym of etre but not the auxiliary

questions.explanation: Motion and state-change verbs such as aller take etre as their auxiliary in the passe compose. The distractors are the default auxiliary for most verbs, an unrelated lexical verb, and a near-synonym that is not the auxiliary.
questions.hint: Verbs of motion and change of state take etre.

uses masculine plural instead of feminine singular

questions.explanation: The adjective agrees with the feminine singular noun maison, so grande is correct. The distractors keep the same root but change gender or number.
